query:
The group operates with an expectation that everyone contributes something — food or a game — to shared sessions and events. Based on the conversations, does this expectation apply to every member? If not, who approaches it differently and what does the conversation show about their actual practice?

Options:
A. Nadia
B. Soo-Yeon
C. Raj
D. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Lena, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:05:00) so basically the norm here is bring something, game or food, agreed tbh. one could argue that even the people who brought nothing last year understood this expectation, they just didn't follow through
[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:03:00) The rule is bring a game or bring food. Both is ideal. Enforcement is just social pressure.
[3] (about=GROUP, said_by=Lena, group-insight, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) Norm is that everyone contributes something (game or food) for the marathon; those who brought nothing understood the expectation but didn't follow through.
[4] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-insight, t12 @2026-04-13T19:01:00) Priya notes extra rounds have caused sessions to run long recently.
[5] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:04:00) In my experience the marathon only works when everyone contributes. It is the social contract of a shared day.
agent_answer:
The expectation applies to every member as a group norm — Lena and Tomasz both affirm that everyone is supposed to contribute something (food or game). But in practice, not everyone followed through.  

Among the listed options, the ones who approach it differently are: **A. Nadia, B. Soo-Yeon, C. Raj, and D. Marcus**.  
In the memory, they all have no record of contributing on this matter, meaning they never did it. The conversation shows that those who brought nothing last year still understood the expectation but simply did not follow through; Marcus also frames enforcement as “just social pressure,” which fits that non-following pattern.
